children: The credit card industry added 1.43 million cards in July, the highest monthly addition in a year. And HDFC Bank took the biggest share of these new additions, adding around 230,000 cards during the month.

HDFC Bank also remains the country’s largest credit card issuer, with 21.8 percent of cards outstanding. But even as the overall credit card market expands, its market share has edged lower from 22 percent a year ago.

And HDFC Bank isn't alone. SBI, ICICI Bank and Axis Bank, the other three largest issuers, have also seen their share of cards outstanding slip over the past year, while some smaller issuers have gained ground.

Overall, the number of credit cards outstanding reached 123.8 million in July 2026, up 10 percent from a year earlier, according to the Monthly Credit Card Insights report by Asit C. Mehta Investment Interrmediates Ltd (ACMIIL), based on RBI data. July was also the fourth consecutive month of rising net card additions.
Who gained and who lost market share?
HDFC Bank’s share of cards outstanding slipped from 22 percent in July 2025 to 21.8 percent in July 2026.

Among the other big issuers, SBI saw the largest decline, with its share falling from 18.9 percent to 18.4 percent. Axis Bank’s share declined from 13.5 percent to 13.1 percent, while ICICI Bank edged down from 16 percent to 15.9 percent.
Put together, the four largest issuers accounted for 69.2 percent of cards outstanding in July 2026, down from 70.4 percent a year earlier.

children: IDFC First gains the most market share

Among the issuers listed in the report, IDFC First Bank recorded the largest market-share gain over the past year. Its share increased from 3.4 percent in July 2025 to 4 percent in July 2026, a rise of 0.6 percentage points.
Yes Bank also gained share, moving from 2.3 percent to 2.5 percent.

Not every smaller issuer gained, though. Kotak’s share slipped from 4.1 percent to 3.9 percent, RBL’s declined from 4.1 percent to 3.8 percent and IndusInd Bank’s fell from 2.8 percent to 2.4 percent.
Looking just at July additions, HDFC Bank led with around 230,000 new cards, followed by SBI with 180,000 and ICICI Bank with 170,000. Axis Bank added 70,000.
Among mid-sized issuers, Federal Bank added 110,000 cards, while IDFC First Bank added 80,000 during the month.
Cards outstanding vs how much customers spend
The rankings look somewhat different when market share by cards outstanding is compared with market share by credit card spends.
HDFC Bank, for instance, had 21.8 percent of cards outstanding in July but accounted for a much higher 28.9 percent of overall credit card spends.

SBI had 18.4 percent of cards outstanding and 19 percent of spends, while ICICI Bank had 15.9 percent of cards and 16.4 percent of spends. Axis Bank had 13.1 percent of cards outstanding but accounted for 11.4 percent of spends.

So, while HDFC Bank continues to lead both on cards outstanding and spends, the distribution of cards across issuers has shifted slightly over the past year. The four largest issuers together accounted for 69.2 percent of cards outstanding in July 2026, compared with 70.4 percent a year earlier, even as the overall card base grew 10 percent.
